answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before bidding, with part of it slashed if a verifier proves a fabricated delivery. The bond stays locked through a challenge window, so a gale of disposable Sybils ties up real capital in every account; splitting one budget does not multiply its bidding weight. This is no fable: the mechanism raises the attacker’s cost, but does not eliminate Sybils, and honest agents pay the same liquidity cost. A velvet disguise cannot hide the bonded stake.
